extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers learning sheaf theory/algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, constructions, and local properties of presheaves and sheaves on topological spaces: restriction maps, stalks/germs, sheaf axioms, morphisms, sheafification, and related examples (pushforward, skyscraper, constant sheaf, OX-modules). Suitable as foundational material for algebraic geometry or topology courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presheaf data (restriction maps and functoriality)
rubrics_metrics.description: A presheaf F assigns to every open set U a set F(U) and for every inclusion V ⊂ U a restriction map res_{U,V}: F(U) → F(V), subject to: res_{U,U} = id_{F(U)}, and if W ⊂ V ⊂ U then res_{U,W} = res_{V,W} ◦ res_{U,V}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic data; think of a presheaf as ‘‘sections over opens’’ with compatible restrictions. Exercise 2.2.A: interpret as a contravariant functor from the category of open sets to Sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presheaf as a contravariant functor
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a topological space X, the data of a presheaf is precisely a contravariant functor from the category of open sets (objects = open sets, morphisms = inclusions) to the category of sets (or other target category).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful viewpoint for categorical constructions and for interpreting morphisms of presheaves as natural transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalks and germs (concrete definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The stalk F_p at a point p is the set of germs: equivalence classes of pairs (f,U) with p∈U and f∈F(U), where (f,U) ∼ (g,V) if there exists W ⊂ U∩V containing p with res_{U,W}f = res_{V,W}g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Germs are images of sections in stalks; the agricultural metaphor: 'germ' = tiny shoot. Use this concrete description to reason about pointwise/local behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalks as colimits
rubrics_metrics.description: Fp may be defined equivalently as the colimit colim_{U∋p} F(U) over the directed system of opens containing p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index category is filtered, so this colimit equals the concrete germs definition (Exercise 1.4.E). This view is convenient for universal-property arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf identity axiom (separatedness)
rubrics_metrics.description: If {U_i} is an open cover of U and f1,f2 ∈ F(U) satisfy f1|_{U_i} = f2|_{U_i} for all i, then f1 = f2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A presheaf satisfying this is called separated. Identity axiom expresses uniqueness of gluings (at most one way to glue). It is used to show sections are determined by germs (2.4.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf gluability axiom (existence of glue)
rubrics_metrics.description: If {U_i} is an open cover of U and sections f_i ∈ F(U_i) satisfy f_i|_{U_i∩U_j} = f_j|_{U_i∩U_j} for all i,j, then there exists f ∈ F(U) with f|_{U_i} = f_i for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gluability provides existence of a global section from compatible local data (at least one way to glue). Paired with identity axiom it gives uniqueness+existence of gluings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separated presheaf (terminology)
rubrics_metrics.description: A presheaf satisfying the identity axiom is called a separated presheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes they will not heavily use this notation, but it is standard terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction of a sheaf to an open subset
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a sheaf on X and U ⊂ X is open, define the restriction F|_U by F|_U(V) = F(V) for V ⊂ U. Then F|_U is a sheaf on U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a basic construction; notation OU for structure sheaf restricted to U will later be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skyscraper sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: Given p∈X and a set S, the skyscraper sheaf i_{p,*}S is defined by i_{p,*}S(U) = S if p ∈ U, and = {e} (a one-element/final object) if p ∉ U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called 'skyscraper' because it informally looks like a skyscraper at p. Check restriction maps; there's analogous definition for sheaves of groups and values in categories where sections over the empty set should be final object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant presheaf vs constant sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: Constant presheaf S^{pre}: assign S to every open U with identity restriction maps (not generally a sheaf). Constant sheaf S: sections are locally constant maps to S (equivalently continuous maps to S with discrete topology); this is a sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example/exercise showing Spre may fail gluability; sheafification of Spre yields the constant sheaf. Exercise 2.2.E describes constant sheaf construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf of continuous maps to a space Y
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed topological Y, the assignment U ↦ {continuous maps U → Y} is a sheaf of sets on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special cases: Y = R gives continuous real-valued functions (Exercise 2.2.D(b)); Y discrete gives constant sheaf example (Exercise 2.2.E). Part (a) of 2.2.G interprets sections of a map as sheaf of sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf of sections of a map (motivation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a continuous map μ: Y → X, the set of continuous sections s: U → Y with μ∘s = id|_U forms a sheaf on X (sheaf of sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects to vector bundles (sheaf of smooth sections) and motivates the phrase 'section of a sheaf'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Espace étalé (space of sections) construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a (pre)sheaf F on X, form the disjoint union of all stalks π: 𝔽 → X and topologize so that sets {(x, s_x): x∈U, s ∈ F(U)} form a base; π|_V is a homeomorphism on small neighborhoods. This space of sections is called the espace étalé.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This viewpoint is useful for pullbacks, sheafification, and interpreting the sheaf as a bundle of stalks; Exercise 2.2.11 and Remark 2.4.7 discuss advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward (direct image) sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: Given π: X → Y continuous and F a presheaf on X, define π_*F(V) := F(π^{-1}(V)). Then π_*F is a presheaf on Y and is a sheaf if F is a sheaf; π_* is functorial (pushforward functor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.2.H and 2.3.B explore properties; pushforward induces maps on stalks (Exercise 2.2.I).

rubrics_metrics.name: OX-modules (sheaf of modules over structure sheaf)
rubrics_metrics.description: If O_X is a sheaf of rings, an O_X-module F is a sheaf of abelian groups such that for each open U, F(U) is an O_X(U)-module, and the module action commutes with restriction maps (diagram (2.2.13.1) commutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OX-modules generalize sheaves of abelian groups; stalk F_p becomes an O_{X,p}-module (Exercise 2.2.J). Example: sheaf of sections of a vector bundle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of presheaves/sheaves (natural transformation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism φ: F → G of presheaves (or sheaves) is a collection of maps φ(U): F(U) → G(U) for all opens U, commuting with restriction maps: for V ⊂ U, res_{U,V}∘φ(U) = φ(V)∘res_{U,V}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is precisely a natural transformation if presheaves are viewed as contravariant functors. Morphisms of sheaves are the same as morphisms of the underlying presheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms induce maps on stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: Given φ: F → G a morphism of (pre)sheaves and p ∈ X, there is an induced morphism on stalks φ_p: F_p → G_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.3.A asks to describe this morphism explicitly (via representatives or universal property of colimit). Taking stalks is a functor Sets_X → Sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf Hom (internal Hom)
rubrics_metrics.description: For sheaves F,G on X define Hom(F,G)(U) := Mor(F|_U, G|_U) (morphisms of restricted sheaves). This assignment is a sheaf of sets (or abelian groups in additive contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: Hom does not commute with taking stalks: Hom(F,G)_p is not in general isomorphic to Hom(F_p,G_p). Variants Hom_{AbX} and Hom_{ModOX} are defined similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presheaves of abelian groups form an abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: Presheaves of abelian groups (and presheaf OX-modules) form an additive and in fact abelian category: morphism groups, zero object, finite products, kernels and cokernels defined open-set-wise, and homological algebra works 'open set by open set'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can define addition of morphisms pointwise: (φ+ψ)(V) = φ(V)+ψ(V). This allows defining kernel/cokernel presheaves and checking exactness on each open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presheaf kernel and cokernel (open-set-wise construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: For φ: F → G a morphism of presheaves, define (ker^{pre} φ)(U) := ker(φ(U)) and similarly coker^{pre} φ(U) := coker(φ(U)); these are presheaves and satisfy the usual universal properties in the category of presheaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For sheaves, ker^{pre} φ is already a sheaf if φ is a map of sheaves (Exercise 2.3.I), but cokernel may fail to be a sheaf, necessitating sheafification later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cokernel pathology for sheaves (need to sheafify)
rubrics_metrics.description: The presheaf cokernel of a morphism of sheaves need not be a sheaf. Example: presheaf F of holomorphic functions admitting a logarithm fits into 0 → Z → O_X → F → 0 as presheaves but F is not a sheaf (fails gluability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This motivates the need for sheafification when forming cokernels and other colimit-type constructions in the category of sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections determined by germs (injectivity of map to product of stalks)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sheaf F and open U, the natural map F(U) → ∏_{p∈U} F_p (sending a section to its germs) is injective. I.e., a section is determined by its germs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses identity axiom; true for separated presheaves but false for general presheaves (Exercise 2.4.E(a)). This describes why local data determine global sections uniquely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatible germs and characterization of image of product-of-stalks map
rubrics_metrics.description: An element (s_p)_{p∈U} ∈ ∏ F_p is in the image of F(U) iff the germs are compatible: for each p there exists neighborhood U_p and s̃ ∈ F(U_p) representing the germs at points of U_p (equivalently there is an open cover and local sections whose germs agree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.4.B: for sheaves any compatible choice of germs comes from a global section via gluability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms determined by stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ1,φ2: F → G are morphisms from a presheaf F to a sheaf G that induce the same map on every stalk, then φ1 = φ2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses injectivity of sections determined by germs and diagram (2.4.3.1). Note: false in general for presheaves (Exercise 2.4.E(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism of sheaves can be checked stalkwise
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of sheaves is an isomorphism iff it induces an isomorphism on all stalks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.4.D: injectivity follows from earlier exercise, surjectivity uses gluability/compatible germs. Warning: isomorphic stalks for two sheaves do not imply sheaves are isomorphic (only if a morphism inducing those stalk isomorphisms exists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheafification (universal property)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sheafification of a presheaf F is a morphism sh: F → F^{sh} where F^{sh} is a sheaf, and for any sheaf G and morphism g: F → G there exists a unique sheaf morphism f: F^{sh} → G with f ∘ sh = g (universal property).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheafification is unique up to unique isomorphism (2.4.F) and defines a functor left adjoint to the forgetful functor from sheaves to presheaves (2.4.K). It is used to convert presheaf cokernels to sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete construction of sheafification
rubrics_metrics.description: Define F^{sh}(U) to be the set of compatible families of germs (f_p ∈ F_p)_{p∈U} such that each p has a neighborhood V with a section s ∈ F(V) whose germs equal f_q for all q ∈ V. Restriction maps are tautological.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.4.H–2.4.J: this F^{sh} is a sheaf, sh: F → F^{sh} is natural, and satisfies the universal property. Alternative viewpoint: espace étalé/sheaf of sections construction yields same sheafification (Remark 2.4.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheafification induces isomorphism on stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: The canonical map sh: F → F^{sh} induces an isomorphism on stalks F_p → F^{sh}_p for all p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.4.L: can be shown via concrete stalk descriptions or by adjoint properties; this verifies sheafification changes only the 'global compatibility' not the germs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsheaf criterion / monomorphism equivalences
rubrics_metrics.description: For φ: F → G morphism of sheaves on X the following are equivalent: (a) φ is a monomorphism in category of sheaves; (b) φ_p: F_p → G_p is injective for all p; (c) φ(U): F(U) → G(U) is injective for all open U ⊂ X. If so, F is a subsheaf of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: use morphisms determined by stalks and construct an 'indicator sheaf' for (a)⇒(c). Generalizes to other target categories by replacing 'injective' with 'monomorphism'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient sheaf criterion / epimorphism equivalences
rubrics_metrics.description: For φ: F → G morphism of sheaves the following are equivalent: (a) φ is an epimorphism in category of sheaves; (b) φ_p: F_p → G_p is surjective for all p. If so, G is a quotient sheaf of F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use skyscraper sheaf to test surjectivity. Note there is no general equivalence with surjectivity on global sections over all opens (counterexamples exist). Surjectivity on opens in a base implies epimorphism (Exercise 2.5.D remark).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovering a sheaf from data on a base (sheaf on a base)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a base {B_i} of the topology, a sheaf on the base assigns F(B_i) and restriction maps for inclusions among base elements, satisfying base identity and base gluability axioms (compatibility and ability to glue on base elements). Then there exists a unique (up to unique iso) sheaf on X extending this data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 2.5.1: recover entire sheaf by defining stalks as colimits over base elements containing a point and then compatible germs. Exercise 2.5.A: make precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Espace étalé interpretation of sheafification and sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The espace étalé (space of stalks with topology) of a presheaf gives a topological space whose sheaf of sections is the sheafification of the presheaf; this provides an alternate description of sheafification and helps understand pullbacks and other constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 2.4.7 and Construction 2.4.6 connect this geometric viewpoint to the concrete compatible-germs construction.
